literal: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi
idiomatic: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

literal: Sun Cen, styled Yanju, was a native of Le'an.
idiomatic: Sun Cen, styled Yanju, came from Le'an.

literal: In youth he steeled his will and studied diligently; from investigating censor he was promoted again to assistant instructor of the National University.
idiomatic: As a youth he disciplined himself in study. From investigating censor he rose to assistant instructor at the National University.

literal: Grand Guardian Cui Guang had him compile the national history; he frequently served as mobile headquarters gentleman and was famed for literary talent.
idiomatic: Grand Guardian Cui Guang put him to work on the national history. He served repeatedly as mobile headquarters gentleman and won renown for his writing.

literal: When Cui Zuchidi rebelled, Cen was involved; he fled to Wang Yuanjing's house and came out only when amnesty was granted.
idiomatic: When Cui Zuchidi rose in rebellion, Cen had been implicated. He hid in Wang Yuanjing's home and emerged only after an amnesty.

literal: Sun Teng recommended him on grounds of kinship, but he was not recognized.
idiomatic: Sun Teng recommended him as a clansman, yet he went unnoticed.

literal: It happened that the Grand Ancestor campaigned west and ascended Fengling; he ordered Li Yishen, director of the central and outer offices, and Li Shilue of the headquarters city bureau jointly to draft a proclamation — both declined and asked that Cen replace them.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched west and climbed Fengling, he ordered Li Yishen of the central and outer offices and Li Shilue of the headquarters city bureau to draft a proclamation together. Both declined and asked that Cen take their place.

literal: The Grand Ancestor brought Cen into the tent, himself blew the fire, and urged him on.
idiomatic: Gao Huan brought Cen into the tent, blew the fire himself, and urged him to write.

literal: Cen took the brush and finished at once; the text was very fine.
idiomatic: Cen took up the brush and finished on the spot; the prose was excellent.

literal: The Grand Ancestor was greatly pleased and at once appointed him chief clerk of the headquarters, in sole charge of documents.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was delighted and immediately made him chief clerk of the headquarters, put exclusively in charge of correspondence.

literal: He could also speak Xianbei and likewise proclaimed orders.
idiomatic: He also knew Xianbei and helped relay commands.

literal: Bearing arduous duties, he was greatly valued and rewarded.
idiomatic: Given the heaviest duties, he was held in exceptional regard.

literal: He was granted Lady Wei as wife — both a scholar's daughter and possessed of beauty; men of the time counted it an honor.
idiomatic: He was given Lady Wei in marriage — a gentleman's daughter, and beautiful besides; contemporaries envied him.

literal: Soon he was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and regularly held the chief clerk post.
idiomatic: Soon he was made left grand master for splendid happiness while continuing as chief clerk.

literal: At first the heir apparent wished to go to Ye and oversee court affairs; the Grand Ancestor, because he was young, did not permit it.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng first wanted to go to Ye to direct government, Gao Huan would not allow it — he was still too young.

literal: Cen spoke on his behalf, and it was indeed carried out.
idiomatic: Cen spoke up for him, and the plan went ahead.

literal: Relying on this he himself asked for extraordinary promotion; the heir apparent only added him as irregular attendant cavalier.
idiomatic: He traded on this favor and asked for extraordinary promotion; Gao Cheng only added the title irregular attendant cavalier.

literal: At the time there was again a great round-up of the people of Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Yu, the two Xia provinces, Gaoping, and Pingliang as soldiers; those who fled and hid — they themselves and their masters, the three heads, and prefectural and county magistrates — were guilty of capital crime, and their households were confiscated.
idiomatic: Another mass levy then swept the people of Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Yu, the two Xia provinces, Gaoping, and Pingliang into the ranks. Anyone who hid — together with his landlord, the three heads of household organization, and local magistrates — faced execution and confiscation of the family property.

literal: Thereupon those seized were very numerous — it was Cen's plan.
idiomatic: The haul was enormous; the scheme was Cen's.

literal: Cen's learning was shallow and his conduct thin; Xing Shao once said to him: "You need to read more.
idiomatic: Cen's learning was shallow and his conduct thin. Xing Shao once told him, "You need to read more.

literal: " Cen said: "My three thousand picked horsemen are enough to match your tens of thousands of weakened troops.
idiomatic: " Cen replied, "My three thousand picked horsemen are enough to match your tens of thousands of worn-out foot soldiers.

literal: " He once took thorn-pill pills; Li He and others teased him, saying: "Your thorns should be enough on their own — why seek outside?
idiomatic: " He once took thorn-pill medicine. Li He and others teased him, "Your thorns ought to be enough on their own — why look elsewhere?

literal: " Those seated all laughed.
idiomatic: " Those present all laughed.

literal: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi summoned Cen to drink; very drunk, he died — aged fifty-two.
idiomatic: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi invited Cen to drink; he drank himself to death, aged fifty-two.

literal: The Grand Ancestor personally attended his funeral.
idiomatic: Gao Huan came in person to mourn him.

literal: Ziru kowtowed asking forgiveness; the Grand Ancestor said: "You have broken my right arm — look up and find me a good replacement and return him to me.
idiomatic: Ziru kowtowed asking forgiveness. Gao Huan said, "You have broken my right arm — find me a good replacement and give him back.

literal: " Ziru recommended Wei Shou; Jishi recommended Chen Yuankang — to succeed Cen.
idiomatic: " Ziru recommended Wei Shou; Jishi recommended Chen Yuankang to succeed Cen.

literal: Posthumously granted equal in protocol to three imperators, minister of personnel, and inspector of Qing Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously granted equal in protocol to three imperators, minister of personnel, and inspector of Qing Province.

literal: As the Grand Ancestor planned the great enterprise, military affairs were numerous and broad; Yuankang received his intent and greatly aided swift execution.
idiomatic: While Gao Huan built his great enterprise amid heavy military burdens, Yuankang carried out his intent and kept affairs moving fast.

literal: By nature he was also gentle and cautious, thoroughly understanding worldly affairs.
idiomatic: Gentle and careful by nature, he understood how things worked in practice.

literal: The Grand Ancestor once grew angry at the heir apparent and within the inner quarters personally beat and kicked him, cursing him to the utmost.
idiomatic: Gao Huan once flew into a rage at Gao Cheng and, in the inner quarters, beat and kicked him while cursing him without restraint.

literal: Coming out he told Yuankang; Yuankang remonstrated, saying: "In teaching and disciplining the heir, there are ritual norms of one's own — deportment and bearing to be looked up to — how can it reach this?
idiomatic: When he came out he told Yuankang. Yuankang remonstrated, "In teaching the heir there are proper ritual norms — conduct others should look up to. How can it go this far?

literal: His words were earnest, even to the point of weeping.
idiomatic: His words were earnest, even to tears.

literal: The Grand Ancestor from this restrained his anger.
idiomatic: From that time Gao Huan checked his anger.

literal: When at times he still raged and beat, he would say: "Do not let Yuankang know.
idiomatic: When he still lashed out in anger, he would say, "Do not let Yuankang know.

literal: " Such was the respect and fear he inspired.
idiomatic: " Such was the regard and restraint he inspired.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, the Grand Ancestor knew it was because of Cui Xuan; he was about to kill Xuan.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Gao Huan knew Cui Xuan was the cause and meant to kill him.

literal: The heir apparent hid him and pleaded on his behalf.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng hid him and pleaded on his behalf.

literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "To spare his life I must still lay hands on him in earnest.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "To spare his life I must still lay on a hard beating.

literal: " The heir apparent thereupon produced Xuan and said to Yuankang: "If you let Cui be caned, we shall not meet again.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng then brought Xuan out and told Yuankang, "If you let Cui be beaten, we are done with each other.

literal: Xuan was in the hall, removing his robe to receive punishment; Yuankang hurried in, mounting the steps in haste, and said: "My lord is about to entrust the realm to the great general — can you not tolerate one Cui Xuan?
idiomatic: " Xuan stood in court stripping off his robe to take punishment. Yuankang rushed in, mounting the steps in haste, and said, "My lord is about to entrust the realm to the great general — can you not tolerate one Cui Xuan?

literal: " The Grand Ancestor followed this and pardoned him.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan followed this and pardoned him.

literal: When the heir apparent entered to assist the capital, Cui Xuan, Cui Jishu, Cui Ang, and others were all employed; Zhang Liang and Zhang Huizuan were both men the Grand Ancestor treated well — yet every commission fell short of Yuankang.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng entered the capital to direct affairs, Cui Xuan, Cui Jishu, Cui Ang, and others were all employed; Zhang Liang and Zhang Huizuan were both men Gao Huan favored — yet every appointment still ranked below Yuankang.

literal: Men of the time said: "The three Cuis and two Zhangs are not the equal of one Kang.
idiomatic: People said at the time, "The three Cuis and two Zhangs are not the equal of one Kang.

literal: " Wei vice director of the masters of writing Lu Daovan of Fanyang had a daughter who was wife to Right Guards General Guo Qiong's son; Qiong was confiscated to the state on a capital charge, and the Grand Ancestor memorialized to grant her to Yuankang as wife — Yuankang thereupon abandoned his former wife, Lady Li, and men of judgment condemned him.
idiomatic: " Wei vice director of the masters of writing Lu Daovan of Fanyang had a daughter married to the son of Right Guards General Guo Qiong. Qiong was condemned to death and his property seized; Gao Huan memorialized to give the woman to Yuankang as wife. Yuankang abandoned his former wife, Lady Li — and men of judgment condemned him.

literal: Yuankang was skilled at winning men's favor, reading faces and awaiting intent; he made many promotions and recommendations, yet could not weigh matters with an even heart, drowning in profit — accepting gold and silk beyond counting, lending on interest and trading across commanderies and counties — and was censured by pure opinion.
idiomatic: Yuankang was skilled at winning favor, reading faces and awaiting intent. He pushed many promotions, yet could not judge fairly, drowning in profit — taking bribes beyond counting, lending at interest and trading across commanderies and counties — and was censured by men of pure judgment.

literal: Following the Grand Ancestor in defeating Zhou Wendi at Mount Mang, he convened the generals in great assembly to deliberate advance and retreat.
idiomatic: After Gao Huan defeated Yuwen Tai of Western Wei at Mount Mang, he convened the generals to debate whether to advance or withdraw.

literal: All held that in the wilds there was no fresh grass, men and horses were worn thin, and distant pursuit was impossible.
idiomatic: All held that the countryside had no fresh forage, men and horses were exhausted, and distant pursuit was impossible.

literal: Yuankang said: "Two heroes have fought for many months; to win a great victory now is heaven's gift — the moment must not be lost; we must press the victory in pursuit.
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Two great rivals have fought for months. To win such a victory now is heaven's gift — the moment must not be lost. We must press the pursuit.

literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "If we meet ambush, how shall I cross over?
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "If we meet ambush, how shall I get through?

literal: " Yuankang said: "When my lord before crossed Shazhi and withdrew the army, they still had no ambush; now they flee defeated like this — how can they plan far?
idiomatic: " Yuankang said, "When you before crossed Shazhi and withdrew, they still laid no ambush. Now they flee in rout like this — how can they plan far ahead?

literal: If you abandon pursuit and do not chase, it will surely become a later trouble.
idiomatic: If you let them go and do not pursue, it will surely breed later trouble.

literal: " The Grand Ancestor in the end did not follow.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan in the end did not follow his advice.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Anping with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed viscount of Anping with three hundred households.

literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and regular palace attendant, transferred to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, and moved to right vice director.
idiomatic: Soon he was made general who pacifies the south and regular palace attendant, transferred to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, then moved to right vice director.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor's illness grew grave, he told the heir apparent: "At the battle of Mount Mang, not using Yuankang's counsel — that is the trouble I bequeath you.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan's illness grew grave, he told Gao Cheng, "At Mount Mang, not taking Yuankang's counsel — that is the trouble I leave you.

literal: With this as regret, I shall die with eyes unclosed.
idiomatic: With this as my regret, I shall die with eyes unclosed."

literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, the death was kept secret and only Yuankang knew.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, the death was kept secret and only Yuankang knew.

literal: The heir apparent succeeded to affairs and again showed him trust and favor.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng succeeded to power and again showed him trust and favor.

literal: He was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and general of the central army, and additionally enfeoffed Duke of Changguo with a fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: He was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and general of the central army, and additionally enfeoffed duke of Changguo with one thousand households.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, the heir apparent, pressed by the generals, wished to kill Cui Xuan to appease them, and spoke of it secretly to Yuankang.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Gao Cheng, pressed by the generals, wished to kill Cui Xuan to appease them and spoke of it secretly to Yuankang.

literal: Yuankang remonstrated, saying: "The four seas are not yet tranquil and the laws are already set — if, because several generals are abroad, you would please their hearts and wrongly kill the innocent, damaging and voiding the penal code, how is it only that you fail heaven above — how can you settle the people below?
idiomatic: Yuankang remonstrated, "The realm is not yet settled and the laws are in place. If, because several generals are in the field, you would please their hearts and wrongly kill the innocent, damaging the penal code — how does that only fail heaven above? How can you settle the people below?

literal: Chao Cuo's affair of old — I beg you, sir, to be cautious.
idiomatic: Chao Cuo's affair of old — I beg you to be cautious.

literal: " The heir apparent thereupon stopped.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon stopped.

literal: Gao Yue campaigned against Hou Jing without success; the heir apparent wished to send Pan Xiangyue as deputy.
idiomatic: Gao Yue campaigned against Hou Jing without success; Gao Cheng wished to send Pan Xiangyue as deputy.

literal: Yuankang said: "Xiangyue is slow in opportune change — Murong Shaozong is better; moreover the former king left a command praising him as able to match Hou Jing. My lord need only place your open heart in this man, and Hou Jing is no cause for worry.
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Xiangyue is slow to adapt — Murong Shaozong is better. Moreover the former king left word that he could match Hou Jing. Place your full trust in this man and Hou Jing need not worry you.

literal: At the time Shaozong was far away; the heir apparent wished to summon and see him, fearing he would be alarmed into rebellion.
idiomatic: Shaozong was then far away; Gao Cheng wished to summon him but feared alarming him into rebellion.

literal: Yuankang said: "Shaozong knows that Yuankang enjoys special regard; he has just sent a man to present gold, to show his sincere allegiance.
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Shaozong knows I enjoy special favor. He has just sent a man with gold to show his sincere allegiance.

literal: Yuankang wished to set his mind at ease, and therefore accepted it while replying to his letter generously.
idiomatic: I wished to set his mind at ease, so I accepted it and replied generously to his letter.

literal: Assuredly there will be no change.
idiomatic: He will surely not waver.

literal: " The heir apparent thereupon entrusted Shaozong, and thereby broke Jing.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon entrusted Shaozong, and thereby defeated Hou Jing.

literal: Yuankang was rewarded with fifty jin of gold.
idiomatic: Yuankang was rewarded with fifty jin of gold.

literal: Wang Sizheng entered Ying city; the generals attacked but could not take it; Yuankang offered a plan to the heir apparent, saying: "My lord assists and steadies court government, yet has no outstanding achievement; though Hou Jing was defeated, he was not a foreign foe in the first place.
idiomatic: Wang Sizheng entered Ying city; the generals attacked but could not take it. Yuankang offered Gao Cheng a plan: "You assist court government yet have no outstanding achievement of your own. Though Hou Jing was defeated, he was never an outside enemy.

literal: Now Ying city is about to fall — I beg my lord to take advantage and press on; that is enough to win prestige and settle your enterprise.
idiomatic: Now Ying is about to fall — take advantage and go in person. That is enough to win prestige and settle your enterprise.

literal: " The heir apparent ordered Yuankang to ride post-horses and observe.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng ordered Yuankang to ride post-horses and observe.

literal: On his return he reported: "It can certainly be taken.
idiomatic: On his return he reported, "It can certainly be taken.

literal: " The heir apparent thereupon campaigned in person; when he arrived it was taken, and Yuankang was rewarded with a hundred ingots of gold.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon campaigned in person; when he arrived the city fell, and Yuankang was rewarded with a hundred ingots of gold.

literal: Earlier, the Wei court had offered the heir apparent the posts of chancellor of state and Prince of Qi; the heir apparent repeatedly declined and would not accept.
idiomatic: Earlier the Wei court had offered Gao Cheng the posts of chancellor of state and Prince of Qi; he repeatedly declined.

literal: He thereupon summoned the generals and Yuankang and others to deliberate in secret; the generals all urged the heir apparent respectfully to accept the court command — Yuankang held it not yet possible.
idiomatic: He then summoned the generals and Yuankang and others to deliberate in secret. The generals all urged Gao Cheng respectfully to accept the court command — Yuankang held it not yet possible.

literal: He also said to Wei Shou: "Looking at these men's words, they mean only to mislead the prince.
idiomatic: He also told Wei Shou, "Judging by what these men say, they mean only to mislead the prince.

literal: I have already memorialized the prince to accept the court command and establish officials; Yuankang, unworthy, might obtain yellow gate gentleman — but the times are not yet right.
idiomatic: I have already told the prince to accept the court command and establish officials — I, unworthy, might obtain yellow gate gentleman — but the times are not yet right.

literal: " Cui Xuan took advantage of the interval to recommend Lu Yuangui as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, intending to divide Yuankang's power.
idiomatic: " Cui Xuan seized the chance to recommend Lu Yuangui as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, intending to divide Yuankang's power.

literal: Yuankang being greedy for goods and bribes, the heir apparent inwardly came gradually to dislike him; Yuankang too was rather afraid.
idiomatic: Because Yuankang was greedy for bribes, Gao Cheng inwardly came to dislike him; Yuankang too grew afraid.

literal: The heir apparent also wished to use him as director of the secretariat, placing him in an idle post — the matter was not carried out.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng also meant to make him director of the secretariat, a post that would sideline him — but the matter was not carried out.

literal: It happened that the heir apparent was about to receive the Wei abdication; Yuankang was with Yang Yin and Cui Jishu in the heir apparent's presence, about to make great transfers and dismissals of court gentlemen, jointly appraising them.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was about to receive the Wei abdication, Yuankang sat with Yang Yin and Cui Jishu in his presence, about to make great transfers and dismissals of court gentlemen, jointly appraising candidates.

literal: The heir apparent's household bondservant Lan Gucheng had earlier managed the kitchen and was greatly favored and intimate.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng's household bondservant Lan Gucheng had earlier run the kitchen and was greatly favored.

literal: Earlier the heir apparent had caned him several dozen times; a man of Wu by nature impetuous, and again relying on old favor, he thereupon grew greatly resentful and with his colleague A Gai plotted to kill the heir apparent.
idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had beaten him several dozen times. A Wu man by nature impetuous, and again relying on old favor, he grew greatly resentful and with his colleague A Gai plotted to kill Gao Cheng.

literal: A Gai then served the Manifest Ancestor, always carrying a knife in attendance, saying: "If you hear shouting from the Eastern Studio," then apply the blade to the Manifest Ancestor.
idiomatic: A Gai then served Gao Yang, always carrying a knife in attendance, saying, "If you hear shouting from the Eastern Studio," then turn the blade on Gao Yang.

literal: That day happened to be when the Wei emperor first established the Eastern Palace and the officials all submitted memorials of congratulation.
idiomatic: That day the Wei emperor had just established the Eastern Palace and officials were submitting congratulatory memorials.

literal: When the affair ended, the Manifest Ancestor went out the Eastern Stop Chariot Gate, bound elsewhere; before he returned the calamity broke out.
idiomatic: When the ceremony ended, Gao Yang went out the Eastern Stop Chariot Gate, bound elsewhere; before he returned the attack began.

literal: Gucheng thereupon came in with food, set a knife beneath the tray, and killed the heir apparent.
idiomatic: Gucheng then came in with food, set a knife beneath the tray, and killed Gao Cheng.

literal: Yuankang used his body to shield and block; he was stabbed, his wounds grave, and died that night — aged forty-three.
idiomatic: Yuankang shielded him with his body; stabbed, gravely wounded, he died that night, aged forty-three.

literal: Yang Yin fled in disarray; Jishu hid in the privy; warehouse attendant Hexi Shele died defending against the assailants.
idiomatic: Yang Yin fled in disarray; Jishu hid in the privy; warehouse attendant Hexi Shele died fighting the assailants.

literal: At the time the heir apparent's violent death was kept secret; therefore Yuankang was buried within the palace, pretended to have been sent on mission to the southern border, and fictitiously appointed director of the secretariat.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng's death was then kept secret; Yuankang was buried in the palace, pretended to have been sent on mission to the southern border, and fictitiously appointed director of the secretariat.

literal: The next year an edict said: "Yuankang's insight surpassed the sages of old, his talent the utmost of the age's heroes — a thousand fathoms none could peer into, ten thousand acres none could fathom.
idiomatic: The next year an edict said, "Yuankang's insight surpassed the sages of old and his talent the flower of the age — a thousand fathoms none could peer into, ten thousand acres none could fathom.

literal: He examined and regulated military government, bound and sustained hegemonic rule, drafted plans at Shaoling's founding, aided at the Henei assembly, devised strategy and settled policy, exerting heart and strength to the full, advancing loyalty and repairing faults, abandoning family and dying for the state, sweeping away fleeing bandits and clearing Jing-Chu — Shen and Fu in elevated Zhou, Zifang in flourishing Han: the same measure across ages, the same beauty across different years.
idiomatic: He examined military government and sustained hegemonic rule, drafted plans at Shaoling's founding and aided at the Henei assembly, devised strategy with all his heart, advanced loyalty and repaired faults, abandoned family and died for the state, swept away fleeing bandits and cleared Jing-Chu — like Shen and Fu in elevated Zhou, like Zifang in flourishing Han: the same measure across ages, the same praise across different years.

literal: The great enterprise was not yet blended; the mountain collapsed and suddenly reached him — grief and mourning being so keen, it is fitting to honor with a rich canon.
idiomatic: The great enterprise was not yet complete when the mountain suddenly collapsed — grief being so keen, it is fitting to honor him with a rich canon.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Yin, and Cang, grand general of agile cavalry, duke of the works, and inspector of Ji Province; posthumously enfeoffed Wuyi County with one thousand households, the former fief remaining as before — posthumous title Wemu.
idiomatic: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, Yin, and Cang provinces, grand general of agile cavalry, duke of the works, and inspector of Ji Province; posthumously enfeoffed Wuyi County with one thousand households, the former fief remaining as before — posthumous title Wemu.

literal: Funeral goods: one thousand two hundred lengths of silk.
idiomatic: Funeral goods: one thousand two hundred lengths of silk.

literal: The grand master of splendid happiness supervised the funeral.
idiomatic: The grand master of splendid happiness supervised the funeral.
